title: Angry relative: a restrained patient
stem: Relatives' room, with a nurse present. A 22-year-old man was brought in by police after chasing people in the street with a chopper while intoxicated. He has been sedated with IM midazolam and is physically restrained while awaiting admission. His mother has arrived. She is shouting that you are imprisoning her son illegally and demands to take him home. Talk to her.
notes:
Checked against NICE NG10 (Violence and aggression, 2015), the Hong Kong Mental Health Ordinance (Cap 136), common-law duty of care, and Hospital Authority policy on restraint.

Conflict resolution: safety first (a nurse or security present, an exit, sit at an angle), introduce yourself, let her speak, acknowledge her feelings (without accepting abuse), explain simply what happened and why he is being looked after, explain the legal and medical basis, involve her in the plan, offer support (medical social worker), set limits calmly if she becomes threatening, and document.

Legal basis: a person who lacks capacity because of intoxication or acute illness can be treated and restrained in their best interests under the common law of necessity, using the least restrictive, proportionate measures, reviewed frequently. If a mental disorder is suspected, the Mental Health Ordinance provides for detention for observation (Section 31, Forms 1–3) or an application to a Magistrate/District Judge. The mother cannot remove an adult who lacks capacity when he is a danger to himself or others.

Your notes list these points (quiet room, empathy, safety of patient, others and mother, the plan, psychiatry, MSW, documentation) — this matches.

steps.label: Before you go in
steps.hint: Safety: a nurse with you, security aware, position near the door.

opts.t: Nurse Ip comes with me; security aware nearby; I'll sit near the door
Go in alone and stand over her
opts.r: Standing over someone escalates; always have a colleague and an exit.

steps.label: Talk to Mrs Lo
steps.hint: Listen, acknowledge, explain, the legal basis, involve her, set limits, support.

turns.line: You've tied up my son like an animal! This is false imprisonment. I'll sue you!

opts.t: I'm Dr Chan, the doctor looking after your son. I can see you're very upset — anyone would be seeing their child like this. Please tell me what worries you most.
opts.r: He's not a criminal! He's my baby!
opts.mark: Introduces self, acknowledges emotion, invites her to speak

opts.t: Calm down or security will remove you.

turns.line: He's not a criminal! He's my baby!

opts.t: We're not treating him as a criminal. When he arrived he'd taken drugs and was trying to hurt people with a knife. We gave him medicine to calm him, and the straps are there only to keep him and the staff safe while it wears off.
opts.r: Drugs? He promised me he stopped…
opts.mark: Explains what happened honestly and why restraint is used

opts.t: He's violent, that's all you need to know.

turns.line: I'm taking him home now. You can't stop me.

opts.t: I understand you want him home. Right now the drugs mean he can't make safe decisions, and he could harm himself or others; the law allows us to care for him until he's safe. We check him every 15 minutes and remove the straps as soon as it's safe. The psychiatrist will see him today.
opts.r: …Will you let me sit with him?
opts.mark: Explains the legal and medical basis and the plan

turns.line: Will you let me sit with him?

opts.t: Yes, when it's safe. I'll also ask our social worker to talk with you — this must be very hard. I'll write down everything we've discussed.
opts.mark: Involves her, offers social work support, documents

qs.q: Legal basis for restraining an intoxicated, dangerous adult who lacks capacity?
qs.a: Common-law necessity, in their best interests, proportionate

qs.q: How often must a restrained patient be reviewed?
qs.a: Frequently (e.g. every 15 minutes) with physical observations
Ensure safety, then listen and acknowledge feelings
IM lorazepam, or IM haloperidol with promethazine
wrong: IV haloperidol alone as first line

qs.q: When should the MHO be considered?
qs.a: When a mental disorder is suspected needing detention

badge.name: Calm Waters
badge.flavor: Safety, listen, acknowledge, explain, involve, support.

options: IM lorazepam, or IM haloperidol plus promethazine
cards.why: Haloperidol alone risks dystonia; check ECG when possible.

options: Avoided even if others are at risk
Calm tone, acknowledge emotion, offer choices

cards.q: Positional asphyxia risk is highest with…
When is a relative entitled to remove an adult patient?
options: Never on their own authority if the adult lacks capacity and is at risk
cards.why: Decisions follow capacity and best interests.
